project.name: Codex of War
project.tagline: Build what the camera can judge.

activeBuild.brief: P00 is accepted as review infrastructure after independent Unity reruns, validation, dashboard checks, and a locked blind baseline comparison.
facts: Two fresh Unity capture-command runs produced the same screenshot SHA-256 a54a917a…4a525aab and render-settings SHA-256 44c656be…73acc12.
Capture self-validation, the standalone validator, all 6 focused EditMode tests, dashboard lint/build, and all 4 dashboard tests passed.
The filed S01 bundle is a 1600×900 Unity 6000.5.4f1 / URP 17.5.0 capture produced with fixed seed 24007001 on Apple M2 / Metal.
The anonymous judge locked Reference 09 (B) over the current Unity frame (A): 76.67 versus 28.33 normalized visual score.
The visual loss is recorded without calling it a win. P00 passes only under its infrastructure exception; every later visual piece must satisfy the full blind-win gate.
The critic assigned exactly one next piece: P10 hero look development, replacing the mannequin proxy with one authored hero mesh and coherent material set.
activeBuild.nextGate: Start P10 only: replace the central hero proxy while freezing the S01 seed, camera, arena, and render settings; file a neutral turntable and fresh deterministic blind-test evidence.

canonicalCapture.name: Explore
canonicalCapture.sceneRead: Foreground, playable stage, and distant silhouette visible
canonicalCapture.benchmarkPolicy: ID only — the local benchmark image is never published

acceptance.blindPreference: New result must win anonymous A/B
acceptance.p00Exception: P00 is an infrastructure gate: its visual baseline comparison is recorded, but a visual loss does not block acceptance when reproducibility, provenance, dashboard delivery, and validation pass.

rounds.label: Round 001
rounds.builderBrief: Wire the deterministic evidence path end to end and produce the first canonical S01 bundle.
rounds.evidence: Two independent Unity reruns matched screenshot and render-settings hashes; validator, 6/6 EditMode tests, and 4/4 dashboard tests passed. The blind visual baseline still lost 28.33–76.67.

critic.primaryGap: The current Unity frame remains a raw blockout: untextured primitive geometry and a mannequin-like hero prevent the focal character and world from reading as production-quality rendered content.

pieces.name: Evidence spine
pieces.outcome: A deterministic review scene, fixed-seed capture command, manifest, round ledger, and live progress surface work end to end.

pieces.name: Shoulder camera
pieces.outcome: Exploration and combat framings preserve subject scale, sightline, collision, target legibility, and authored camera presets.

pieces.name: Ground locomotion
pieces.outcome: Walk, run, pivot, stop, strafe, slope handling, and camera-relative control have grounded acceleration and readable weight.

pieces.name: Hero animation foundation
pieces.outcome: Idle, locomotion, pivots, combat stance, weapon handling, additive aim, and transitions share coherent body mechanics.

pieces.name: Light combo
pieces.outcome: Buffered three-hit chain has authored startup, active, recovery, and cancel windows with one-hit-per-target resolution.

pieces.name: Heavy attack
pieces.outcome: Heavy strike communicates commitment, displacement, contact, hitstop, camera impulse, and enemy reaction.

pieces.name: Dodge and evasion
pieces.outcome: Directional dodge, invulnerability window, recovery, and camera continuity are predictable and readable.

pieces.name: Hit reaction and death
pieces.outcome: Zombies react by hit direction and severity, preserve contact, stagger, collapse, and settle without foot sliding or explosive ragdolls.

pieces.name: Zombie navigation
pieces.outcome: One zombie can acquire, approach, flank, telegraph, attack, recover, lose or reacquire, and die without navigation jitter.

pieces.name: Crowd combat director
pieces.outcome: Four-to-six zombies surround without dog-piling; attack tokens, spacing, off-screen pressure, and threat cues create readable crowd combat.

pieces.name: Hero look development
pieces.outcome: The first anime-style fighter reads as a premium authored character at gameplay and finisher distance, with coherent skin, hair, cloth, metal, and weapon materials.

pieces.name: Zombie look development
pieces.outcome: The zombie archetype and variants have layered anatomy, clothing history, damage language, silhouette variation, and material response.

pieces.name: Arena composition
pieces.outcome: A compact arena has foreground framing, combat stage, silhouette depth, traversal logic, landmarks, and no empty test-level read.

pieces.name: Lighting and atmosphere
pieces.outcome: Key, fill, rim, exposure, fog, shadows, grading, and local reactive light keep faces and contact readable while creating depth.

pieces.name: Combat VFX
pieces.outcome: Weapon trails, contact flash, sparks, debris, blood or dust, and lingering particles form a restrained macro, impact, and decay stack anchored to motion.

pieces.name: Combat audio
pieces.outcome: Foley, effort, weapon movement, contact, zombie vocals, ambience, music, ducking, and spatial mix support timing and impact.

pieces.name: HUD and threat language
pieces.outcome: Minimal health, ability, lock-on, and threat information remains legible without weakening the cinematic frame.

pieces.name: Finisher vignette
pieces.outcome: A contextual finisher has reliable setup, three-character blocking when relevant, facial and contact framing, camera choreography, and clean return to play.

pieces.name: Integrated encounter
pieces.outcome: A polished 45–90 second encounter combines the accepted systems into one authored dramatic arc.

pieces.name: Performance and delivery
pieces.outcome: The native macOS target runs reliably, captures deterministically, meets frame budgets, and ships with reproducible build instructions.

pieces.name: Fighter contract
pieces.outcome: Data-driven fighter, weapon, and ability definitions support selection without branching the shared combat core.

pieces.name: Fighter two
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Fighter three
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Fighter four
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Roster select and persistence
pieces.outcome: Selection, preview, input, save or load, and per-fighter progression work coherently.

pieces.name: Roster encounter balance
pieces.outcome: All fighters can complete the benchmark encounter while remaining mechanically and audiovisually distinct.
